security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives caused by placeholders, Markdown formatting, documented configuration paths, and dense Chinese text. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found. Three medium risks remain: automatic cloud upload of local media, unpinned global package installation, and API keys in command arguments.

remediation.issue: Cloud mode uploads local media files before processing.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before each local-file upload and clearly state the destination, retention policy, and available local alternative.

remediation.issue: The installation command resolves an unpinned package globally.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited package version, document integrity verification, and request confirmation before changing the global Node.js environment.

remediation.issue: Initialization examples place the API key in command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Use an environment variable, standard input, or a secure credential store so secrets do not enter process arguments or shell history.

semantic_findings.title: Local Media Uploaded in Cloud Mode
semantic_findings.description: Cloud mode accepts local media paths and uploads those files before submitting jobs, creating an external data-transfer risk without an explicit consent step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly states that local media paths are uploaded before cloud submission. The transfer is intended but can expose sensitive media if users do not confirm it.

semantic_findings.description: The setup guide recommends a global, unpinned npm installation, which modifies the host and trusts whichever package version resolves at execution time.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command installs @volcengine/mediakit-cli globally without a version or integrity constraint. This creates a clear supply-chain and host-modification risk.

content.user_title: Process and Analyze Video with MediaKit
content.value_statement: Complex video workflows often require separate tools and manually assembled commands. This skill selects MediaKit capabilities, builds valid CLI calls, and guides asynchronous result retrieval.
actual_capabilities: Submit MediaKit cloud jobs and retrieve asynchronous results by task identifier.
Create timestamped subtitles from speech and recognize text visible in video frames.
Analyze storylines and identify highlight moments in dramas and game recordings.
Enhance video quality with standard or generative restoration settings.
Remove hard subtitles or produce transparent video through background matting.
Probe video metadata and divide videos into scenes using configurable thresholds.
limitations: MediaKit CLI must be installed, and most capabilities require network access and a valid cloud API key.
Most operations are asynchronous and require task polling before final media or analysis results are available.
Cloud mode may upload local media files to the MediaKit service for processing.
Input size, duration, format, and local execution support vary by capability.

use_cases.title: Prepare Accessible Video
use_cases.description: Generate timed speech subtitles or extract visible on-screen text for review and localization.

use_cases.title: Create Promotional Highlights
use_cases.description: Find strong drama or gameplay moments and produce structured highlight selections or edited outputs.

use_cases.title: Automate Media Quality Checks
use_cases.description: Inspect metadata, detect scene boundaries, and submit enhancement jobs within repeatable media pipelines.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Use MediaKit to inspect the metadata for [video URL]. Report resolution, frame rate, bitrate, codecs, duration, and any processing constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Create Timed Subtitles
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate [language] subtitles from [video or audio URL]. Enable speaker labels and confidence scores, then retrieve the completed task result.

prompt_templates.title: Enhance and Segment Footage
prompt_templates.prompt: Enhance [video URL] for the [scene type] scenario at [resolution], then segment scenes between [minimum] and [maximum] seconds.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Highlight Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [video URLs] using the [drama or game] model. Define highlight criteria, preserve one client token per retry, poll completion, and summarize outputs.

output_examples.input: Inspect the metadata of a public training video and summarize its technical properties.
output_examples.output: The inspection task completed. The report lists container format, duration, resolution, frame rate, bitrate, and video and audio codecs.

output_examples.input: Create Chinese speech subtitles with speaker labels and confidence scores.
output: The transcription job was submitted and tracked to completion.
The result contains timestamped subtitle segments, detected speakers, and confidence values.

output_examples.input: Find gameplay highlights and create an edited promotional video.
output_examples.output: The completed result identifies key gameplay moments and provides the generated highlight video with supporting clip information.

best_practices: Confirm cloud processing and local-file upload with the user before submitting private or licensed media.
Reuse the same client token for retries, and create a new token only for an intentional rerun.
Check each capability's input limits, supported formats, execution mode, and mutually exclusive parameters before submission.
anti_patterns: Do not place API keys directly in prompts, command arguments, logs, or callback values.
Do not submit inaccessible URLs or assume every capability supports local execution.
Do not repeatedly create new tasks while an existing asynchronous task is still processing.

faq.question: Does this skill process video locally?
faq.answer: Most capabilities are cloud only. Green-screen matting and metadata probing document local support, with additional local format and dependency constraints.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: Cloud mode requires a MediaKit API key. Store it in the supported environment or credential configuration instead of command arguments.

faq.question: Can I provide a local media file?
faq.answer: Cloud mode can upload a local path before processing. Confirm the transfer and review data handling requirements before using sensitive media.

faq.question: Why does the first command return only a task identifier?
faq.answer: Most video operations are asynchronous. Query the returned task identifier until MediaKit reports completion and provides the final result.

faq.question: Which video analysis features are available?
faq.answer: The skill covers subtitles, OCR, storylines, highlights, metadata, scene segmentation, enhancement, subtitle removal, and background matting.

faq.question: How should failed jobs be retried?
faq.answer: Reuse the original client token for a retry. Use a new unique token only when you intend to create a separate execution.
